judged_text: The handler commits the new attendee rows via prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar update (line 165) and email send (line 168) run, with no transaction, compensation, or attendee-removal path. When eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees fails (expired OAuth credential, provider error, already-deleted external event), the guests are already persisted, the client sees an error, and resubmitting the same emails is rejected by the uniqueGuests filter with emails_must_be_unique_valid — the booking is left with guests who never reached the external calendar or their inbox, and the organizer has no indication that resubmitting with one extra email is the only recovery.

When eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees fails (expired OAuth credential, provider error, already-deleted external event), the guests are already persisted, the client sees an error, and resubmitting the same emails is rejected by the uniqueGuests filter with emails_must_be_unique_valid — the booking is left with guests who never reached the external calendar or their inbox, and the organizer has no indication that resubmitting with one extra email is the only recovery.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and before sending emails. There is no transaction/rollback/compensation if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it’s not wrapped in try/catch), so the mutation can fail after guests are already stored. On retry, the handler re-fetches the booking (now containing those persisted attendees) and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing `booking.attendees`, which can make `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throw `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). This matches the finding: DB ends up updated while external calendar/email side effects may not have occurred, with no recovery path in the handler.
